svg.aria-label: The openCypher subset engine: query text parsed by the ANTLR M23 grammar into our own AST and evaluated in memory over a read-only BookGraph; unsupported syntax refused with its position; the supported and refused lists; the committed queries as the spec
svg.text: A SUBSET OF OPENCYPHER, IN MEMORY · src/TemporalGraph.Query · READ-ONLY
loaded read-only from a book file
~0.1 s a query after a ~0.5 s warm-up
SUPPORTED · WHAT THE COMMITTED QUERIES NEED, AND NOTHING MORE
MATCH / OPTIONAL MATCH with comma patterns · one label · inline property maps
WHERE: comparisons · AND OR NOT · IS [NOT] NULL · IN · STARTS WITH · CONTAINS · parameters
WITH … WHERE · RETURN … AS · DISTINCT · ORDER BY · SKIP · LIMIT
count · collect · id · type · labels · coalesce
null, equality and ordering follow the openCypher CIP on comparability and orderability
the engine is described as “a subset of openCypher”
Nine committed queries in queries/hound-of-the-baskervilles/, grown to twelve per book with the chat's tools; the three books' folders are kept identical.
The API binds $pos, $chapter, $character, $spoilers. No hidden time filter: ($spoilers OR r.revealedPos <= $pos) is in the query text.
Eight samples per book with literal names (“Whom has Dr. Watson met so far?”), still gated by $pos and $spoilers; all 24 return rows and a test runs every one.
A run lights its nodes and edges in the graph tabs; the grid hides id columns unless “Show ids” is ticked.
Alternatives: Cyphoid returns null for a relationship variable (our time data is on edges);
LadybugDB's .NET binding lags the engine; Kùzu and openCypherTranspiler are archived;
GraphQLite has no .NET binding. Translating to SQL only if a book outgrows memory.
